views.alt: Cloudflare's deploy form, with no Git account yet

steps.html: In Cloudflare's form, under Git account, click New GitHub connection.

views.alt: GitHub asking to install and authorize Cloudflare Workers and Pages

steps.html: GitHub asks to install Cloudflare Workers and Pages. Keep All repositories: the deploy creates a new repository.
Click Install & Authorize.

views.alt: Cloudflare's own Select a repository page

steps.html: Cloudflare then opens its own Select a repository page. Ignore it: close this tab.

views.alt: The deploy form with a GitHub account picked, the project name, SETUP_MODE and the Deploy button

steps.html: Click Deploy to Cloudflare on this page again. Under Git account, pick your GitHub account: it's in the list now.
Keep the project name comfy-gen.
SETUP_MODE holds your answer from this page: leave it as it is.
Click Deploy.

views.alt: The finished build in Cloudflare, with its green tick

steps.html: The build runs for about a minute. When it shows a green tick (Success), reload the page.

views.alt: The Worker's page in the Cloudflare dashboard, with its Visit button

steps.html: Click Visit (top right). That's your Worker, at https://comfy-gen.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev: bookmark it.

views.alt: Cloudflare's Create Token page, filled in, with the Continue to summary button

steps.html: The permissions are already filled in. If your Cloudflare login also belongs to other accounts (an employer's, say), change All accounts to your own, so the token can't touch them.
Scroll down and click Continue to summary.

views.alt: The token summary, with the Create Token button

steps.html: Click Create Token.

views.alt: The new token, shown once, with its copy button

steps.html: Copy the token with the button at its end, and paste it below.

views.alt: R2's page before it is turned on, with the Add R2 subscription to my account button

steps.html: Click Add R2 subscription to my account. It's $0 due; if the account has no card, it asks for one first.

views.alt: The Cloudflare dashboard's sidebar, with Manage account open

steps.html: In the Cloudflare dashboard's sidebar, open Manage account…
…then Billing.

views.alt: Cloudflare's billing page, on Billable usage

steps.html: Open Billable usage…
…then Budget alerts.

views.alt: Cloudflare's default $10 budget alert

steps.html: Cloudflare made a $10 alert already. To change the amount, click the pencil. It only emails you: it never stops anything.

views.alt: Modal's Usage & billing settings, with Manage payment details

steps.html: In Modal, open Settings → Usage & billing and click Manage payment details to add a card.

views.alt: Modal's Usage limit tab, with Edit spend limit

steps.html: In Settings → Usage & billing, open the Usage limit tab.
Click Edit spend limit: past the free credits, Modal stops all work at that amount. At $0 you never pay past them.

views.alt: Modal's API tokens settings, with the New Token button

steps.html: In Modal's Settings, open API tokens & service users.
Click New Token.

views.alt: Modal's New token dialog

steps.html: Click Create token. The name is optional.

views.alt: The new token, inside a modal token set command

steps.html: Modal shows the token once, inside a command. Copy the whole command (hover it for the copy button) and paste it into Modal command below.

views.alt: claude.ai's Customize, on Connectors

steps.html: In claude.ai, click Customize in the sidebar.
Open Connectors.

views.alt: The Add menu, with Add custom connector

steps.html: Click Add…
…then Add custom connector.

views.alt: The Add custom connector dialog, empty

steps.html: Name it anything (Comfy-Gen, say).
Paste your connector URL (Copy URL, above).
Click Continue.

views.alt: The dialog's second page, with No sign-in picked

steps.html: Under Authentication, keep No sign-in. Its warning, that anyone with the URL can use the connector, is expected: the URL is the secret.
Scroll down and click Add.

views.alt: The new connector's page, with its Connect button

steps.html: Click Connect.

views.alt: A new chat's + menu

steps.html: In a chat, click +…

views.alt: The Connectors submenu, with the connector turned on

steps.html: …open Connectors…
…and turn your connector on.
Ask for an image. The first time, Claude asks to allow the tool: choose Always allow.

views.alt: The agent's page, with the Pairing link field and the Pair button

steps.html: The agent's page opens in your browser. Paste the pairing link (Copy link, above) into Pairing link.
Click Pair.

views.alt: macOS's warning that it could not verify comfy-gen-agent

steps.html: Unzip comfy-gen-agent-macos.zip and open comfy-gen-agent. macOS says it can't verify it: click Done.

views.alt: System Settings, Privacy & Security, with Open Anyway

steps.html: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and scroll down to Security.
Next to the note that comfy-gen-agent was blocked, click Open Anyway, and enter your password.

views.alt: macOS asking once more

steps.html: macOS asks once more: click Open Anyway. From then on it opens normally.
